fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Greedy regular expression matching
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: @inproceedings{frischCardelli, title = {Greedy Regular Expression Matching}, author = {Frisch, Alain and Cardelli, Luca}, year = {2004}, isbn = {978-3-540-27836-8}, booktitle = {Automata, Languages and Programming}, editor = {D{\'i}az, Josep and Karhum{\"a}ki, Juhani and Lepist{\"o}, Arto and Sannella, Donald}, pages = {618--629}, publisher = {Springer Berlin Heidelberg}, address = {Berlin, Heidelberg}, abstract = {This paper studies the problem of matching sequences against regular expressions in order to produce structured values.} }

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: A regular expression r may be unambiguous. To resolve this unambiguity one may choose to instead replace r with an unambiguous goal for parsing, or instead one may define a disambiguation strategy for r.

For instance, in Greedy regular expression matching Frisch and Cardelli alleviate the ambiguity of parsing a Kleene star by always taking the cons branch when possible. That is, when scanning over a string left-to-right with the goal of parsing a Kleene star of A and then another grammar B, we greedily parse a Kleene star of maximal length before moving on to a B.

This same greediness approach is common in parsing theory. It is also used in Regular expression containment: Coinductive axiomatization and computational interpretation and in parsing expression grammars.
